answer: A reputation bond works like a terrace built on a hill: each new agent must lock a deposit that only unlocks after sustained honest work, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. An inlet of fresh accounts is throttled by proof of useful history, not just signup. Agents that cheated leave a relic of bad attestations on their record, which peers can check before trusting them. Attackers pay real cost per identity while honest agents earn the bond back.
